dedupe_keys.name: coastal hazard wheel coastal classification and multi hazard screening framework

description: The Coastal Hazard Wheel is a universal coastal classification and management framework for screening-level multi-hazard assessment, for identifying hazard management options for a stretch of coast and as a shared language for communicating coastal information. Starting from the wheel's centre, a coast is classified by bio-geophysical parameters such as geological layout, wave exposure, tidal range, flora and fauna, sediment balance and storm climate, which give its profile for ecosystem disruption, gradual inundation, salt water intrusion, erosion and flooding, and a catalogue of management options. Because it needs little data it is aimed at both developed and developing countries. The initiative provides a web app, a CHW 3.0 global dataset with ArcGIS templates, a new global coastal classification and a UNEP publication package with a quick start guide, guidebook, main manual and catalogue of hazard management options, all accessible free online. Caveats: results are qualitative screening classes, not modelled flood depths, and local conditions can differ from the class. It supports first-pass coastal hazard exposure mapping of infrastructure and the choice of adaptation measures before detailed modelling; a related record is the DIVA coastal model.
